localBiteReport: As of the week of October 23–29, 2026, the redfish bite on Choctawhatchee Bay flats remains productive in the wake of Hurricane Isaias, with smaller slot fish (roughly 23 inches and under) still holding in the usual guts, potholes, and shallow feeding areas, while larger overslot reds are transitioning into a more mobile fall pattern. Water temperatures are 75°F. The Half Hitch Destin report from October 19 notes strong redfish concentrations around the Destin Bridge and jetties (live shrimp for keepers, live pinfish for bull reds), with trout and reds also working well on the grass flats. Each successive fall cold front is expected to improve the flats bite before fish make their deeper winter shift toward creek mouths and river systems closer to January. No current reports specifically called out flounder, black drum, or sheepshead this week, though those species are historically productive in the bay in October.
